title: Percentage of Financial Crime Cases with Confiscated Assets Returned to Victims and Forfeited by Government
what_it_is: Percentage of Financial Crime Cases with Confiscated Assets Returned to Victims and Forfeited by Government

sections.label: Financial crime asset restitution questions
sections.summary: An MP asked about restitution percentages, forfeited scam proceeds, and measures ensuring victims receive restitution before funds go to the consolidated fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what percentage of financial crime cases that involve confiscated assets result in full or partial restitution to victims; (b) what proportion of seized scam proceeds in the past five years have been forfeited to the state rather than returned to victims; and (c) what measures are in place to ensure that all reasonably identifiable scam victims receive restitution before funds are transferred to the Government's consolidated fund.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: When investigating financial crime cases, the Police would freeze bank accounts and seize any assets suspected to be proceeds of crime or which constitute evidence.

sections.label: Gazette notice and forfeiture process
sections.summary: Police publish a Gazette notice giving six months to claim seized property, which is forfeited only if unclaimed; tracking scam proceeds is operationally challenging.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: Where the persons entitled to the seized property cannot be ascertained or found, the Police would publish a notice in the Government Gazette to request for persons to establish their claim to the property within six months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The seized property would only be forfeited to the state if no one establishes a claim after the six-month notice period.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: It is operationally challenging to apportion and thus track the amount of scam proceeds returned to victims or forfeited to the state.

sections.label: Tracking amounts feasibility study
sections.summary: The Ministry of Home Affairs will explore the feasibility of tracking these amounts in the longer term.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Home Affairs will explore the feasibility of tracking these amounts in the longer term.

sections.label: Scam losses and recovery figures
sections.summary: Total losses this year are $1.1 billion while monies recovered are $182 million, a fraction of the total lost.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: The next point I would like to add is that, as you can tell from the latest numbers, total losses are $1.1 billion this year; monies recovered this year are $182 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: It is a fraction of the total amounts of monies lost.
